summary: Move all zeros to the end of the array in place while keeping the order of non-zero elements.
mainInsight: Maintain a write index j for the next non-zero position; every non-zero element is moved (swapped) there, which pushes zeros toward the end automatically while preserving order.

approaches.name: Write pointer + swap
approaches.summary: For each non-zero nums[i] swap with nums[j] and j += 1.

approaches.name: Write pointer + fill zeros
approaches.summary: Copy non-zeros forward, then fill the remainder with 0.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Skip the swap when i == j to avoid redundant writes.

promptVariants: Which pattern solves Move Zeroes in place?
What is the same technique as Remove Element?
cards.explanation: A write index tracks the boundary between the non-zero prefix and the zeros.

promptVariants: What does nums[0..j-1] and nums[j..i-1] look like during the loop?
Describe the regions of the array while the Move Zeroes loop is running.
cards.answer: nums[0..j-1] are the non-zero elements seen so far in original order; nums[j..i-1] are all zeros. Swapping a new non-zero with nums[j] keeps both properties.
keyPoints: Between j and i: only zeros
cards.explanation: That is why a swap (not an overwrite) leaves the zeros behind.

promptVariants: Move Zeroes in a single pass is ___ time.
Move Zeroes in place uses ___ extra space.
When i == j the swap is a no-op. How could you avoid unnecessary writes, and why does the order stay stable?
Why does the swap-based Move Zeroes preserve the order of non-zero elements, and how would you skip redundant swaps?
cards.answer: Skip the swap when i == j (nothing but non-zeros so far), or overwrite nums[j] = nums[i] and fill zeros afterwards. The order stays stable because non-zero elements are moved forward in the order they are encountered.
cards.explanation: Swapping is equivalent to compaction here.

promptVariants: What happens for an array without zeros?
options: [0,0,1] stays unchanged because zeros are already first
[0,1,0] with the single 1 pulled into the middle
It raises an error because no zero is found to swap with
cards.explanation: With no zeros i and j move together (self-swaps); with leading zeros the first non-zero is swapped to the front.
